title: Evergreen Analytics pilot call — working journal
body:
Summary: quick capture from kickoff call with Evergreen Analytics (EA). Customer is a data-platform company doing internal search + insights over proprietary market datasets. They want fast local vector search + generation for analyst workflows. Mix of browser UI and internal APIs.

Attendees: Evergreen - Nora Diaz (CTO), James Ho (Infra), Alina Rhee (Data Platform); Redwood - Samira (SE), Ethan (SRE), Priya (Product).

Primary asks / goals:
- Pilot: private deployment (VPC) in AWS account; must not send data to hosted plane.
- Use-cases: semantic search (embeddings) + short generative answers for analysts (2–4 sentence summaries).
- Latency targets: interactive UX target p50 <= 60ms for embeddings lookup (service + kNN), p50 <= 150ms for short generation (<= 256 tokens). They emphasized perceived snappiness.
- Throughput: expected 200–400 QPS for embeddings during business hours; generation spikes to ~80 rps in peak. Burst tolerance required.
- Models: prefer open models. They mentioned 7B and 13B tiers; evaluate 13B quantized to int8/4. Interested in Redwood-recommended variant with quantization + hardware pairing.
- Security/compliance: customer holds sensitive vendor contract data; data residency in us-west-2; want KMS integration + HSM option later; strict audit logs and key rotation policy.

Technical notes / gotchas observed:
- Document corpus has many long documents (avg 12k tokens) but queries are short; need effective chunking strategy and embedding pipeline. Risk: naive chunking creates noisy retrieval; recommend context-aware chunker (sentence + overlap) and per-chunk metadata.
- High variance in seq lengths — runtime should handle dynamic batch sizing without blowing latency SLOs. If batch windows are tuned for throughput, generation latency may spike.
- They will likely want streaming completions in the UI to improve UX. Check compatibility with the on-prem runtime for streaming + function-calls.
- Embeddings indexing: they plan to use a managed vector DB but are open to using our suggestions (we should list Faiss/Annoy/ScaNN + performance notes). Need to confirm whether they want Redwood to host index or keep local.
- Tokenization: vendor data contains code-like snippets and ticked segments; some models handle code tokens differently — evaluate tokenizer mismatch.
- Cost sensitivity: EA asked for rough cost-per-query estimates and a reference bill for expected QPS. They will compare Dedicated vs Private pricing.

Open questions to resolve (short list):
1) Do they require air-gapped on-prem eventually or only VPC in AWS? Nora said "maybe" for on-prem later — capture as long-term requirement.
2) What is SLA expectation for pilot? They asked what Redwood can guarantee for latency during pilot. We should propose internal SLOs for canary stage.
3) Embedding dimension preference? EA currently uses 1024-d vectors in their legacy system; we need to map model embedding dims to their index strategy.
4) Data retention / logs: what minimum retention for query logs is acceptable? They want immediate opt-out for specific datasets.

Immediate next steps (owner):
- (Samira) Send follow-up email with pilot scope doc draft + minimal architecture sketch (by 2025-02-13). Include two routing options: dedicated pool vs private VPC with dedicated nodes.
- (Ethan) Open SRE ticket to validate VPC peering patterns and necessary firewall rules for private control plane; list required ports and NAT expectations (by 2025-02-14). Link: JIRA-ENG-1178.
- (Priya) Prepare cost/ops model with ballpark numbers for embeddings + gen at expected QPS, include Dedicated monthly commit vs pay-as-you-go in private (by 2025-02-18).
- (Marius) Spin up eval harness PR with sample prompts and long-doc chunking tests for 13B int8 variant; include tokenization edge cases (by 2025-02-20). GH: gh:redwood-inference/eval-harness#42.
- (Samira) Draft NDA clause addition re: ephemeral log storage and retention controls (send to legal) (by 2025-02-16).

Experiment ideas / quick wins to propose:
- Try embeddings+FAISS local index with dynamic re-ranking using small generative model for final answer (faster than full generation).
- Enable KV/prefix caching for repeated analyst queries to reduce cost.
- Suggest hybrid routing: use cheaper 7B variant for low-confidence retrievals; route to 13B for fallback. Need to validate hallucination/regression risk.

Risks / escalation items:
- If we under-provision GPU memory for int8 13B with large kv cache, migrations will be disruptive. Prioritize memory footprint reports per candidate model.
- Networking: customer's restrictive egress policy may block outbound to control plane. Need plan B (bring control plane into their VPC or temporary exposed endpoints).
- Eval leakage: test data contains PII; ensure eval harness scrubs or is run in their environment.

Notes to self / rough timeline:
- Week 1: pilot architecture + cost overview + SRE kickoff.
- Week 2: eval harness + sample dataset ingestion test (on their staging S3).
- Week 3: small canary rollout (1 shard) with telemetry & tracing in Redwood Console.
- Week 4–6: iterate on quantization profile, caching knobs, and perf tuning.

Meeting artifacts to attach to Confluence page: call recording link, Nora's deck (they promised), sample dataset S3 prefix, NDA draft.

One-off comments: Nora stressed analyst workflow latency more than absolute token cost. They will accept slightly higher unit cost if UX is smooth. Good justification for streaming + prefix caching.

End of notes.

TODO (quick): compose email + attach pilot-arch sketch, create Confluence page stub, assign SRE ticket, link GH eval PR.
